overview: Laboratory Sample Traceability and Rework addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in healthcare providers operations. The first proof of value uses specimen IDs, analyser quality flags and courier checkpoints. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is recollected specimens per 1,000, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: specimen IDs, analyser quality flags and courier checkpoints; define recollected specimens per 1,000 and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hospital COO / Chief Medical Information Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
